title: Regional onboard priority & warmpool allocation — Q3 2026
content:
Purpose: This is an operational capacity sheet for Q3 2026 that proposes a prioritized regional onboarding sequence, warmpool (idle reserved capacity) sizing, and per-region buffer allocation for our multi-cloud GPU fleet. Focus is to minimize cold-start exposure for enterprise Dedicated customers while keeping unit cost within current target bands (hosted target $/token +- 12%).

Executive summary:
- Approach: Two-stage activation (initial wave + steady-state warmpool) with staggered week-by-week onboarding windows per region to reduce cross-region supply pressure.
- Target outcome: Maintain >=95% probability of meeting 99th percentile latency SLOs for priority customers while keeping warmpool idle fraction <= 18% fleet-wide.
- Time horizon: July 2026 — December 2026 (detailed weekly cadence for Q3 presented below).

Key assumptions:
- Lead time for new reserved instances or private on-prem racks = 6–8 weeks from order to ready. Cloud SKU availability (H100, A100) may vary by region and vendor; assume 10% SKU substitution allowed.
- Average utilization target for hosted workloads once warmed = 72% (token-weighted). Dedicated pools target = 78% steady-state.
- Warmpool sizing aims to cover 14-day stochastic surge at 60th–90th percentile depending on customer tier and region.
- Spot/variable capacity is treated as 1.0x equivalent to reserved capacity for planning, but only 55% reliable for critical Dedicated lanes.

Regional priority (high-level rationale):
1) NA (Bay and east US zones) — high inbound demand growth, multiple anchor enterprise customers, fastest onboarding cadence.
2) EU (West/Central) — predictable enterprise demand but longer procurement windows and stricter compliance; maintain larger warmpool for private lanes.
3) APAC (Japan, Singapore) — accelerating demand but constrained SKU availability; phase activation to rely on burst routing to NA for 6 weeks while local capacity ramps.

Per-region capacity plan (summarized numbers for Q3 onboarding waves):
- NA (Jul 1 -> Sep 30): Planned additions = 1,200 GPUs total (wave breakdown: Jul-week2 300, Jul-week6 300, Aug-week2 300, Sep-week1 300). Warmpool target = 16% of NA fleet (~192 GPUs) to cover enterprise spikes and predictable morning windows. Warmpool composition: 60% reserved, 40% spot for cost flexibility.
- EU (Jul 15 -> Oct 15): Planned additions = 640 GPUs (Jul-week4 160, Aug-week3 160, Sep-week2 160, Oct-week2 160). Warmpool target = 20% (~128 GPUs), with preference for reserved and private-deploy capacity due to regulatory SLAs.
- APAC (Aug 1 -> Nov 1): Planned additions = 480 GPUs (Aug-week2 120, Sep-week1 120, Sep-week4 120, Oct-week3 120). Warmpool target = 18% (~86 GPUs), heavier reliance on burst to NA during early weeks.

Warmpool sizing rationale and micro-buffering:
- We use a layered buffer: global emergency buffer (fleet-level) = 125 GPUs; regional warmpool = per-region % above. Regional micro-buffers (per-zone within region) = 10–12% of regional warmpool to accommodate Zonal failures or maintenance windows.
- Warmpool replenishment policy: automated top-up when active warmpool utilization falls below 65% of target for 24h (trigger creates incremental provisioning request).

Cost and utilization tradeoffs (high-level):
- Idle warmpool cost estimate: NA warmpool monthly run cost ~ $220k (mix weighted across H100/A100 spot/reserved).
- Expected net uplift in SLA-compliant revenue from warmpool enabled rollouts estimated to offset ~60–80% of incremental cost in first 90 days (conservative estimate based on historical churn).

Rolling timeline (detailed weekly cadence for Q3 2026):
- Week 1 (Jul 1–7): NA wave0 prep: vendor confirmations, final SKU allocation, warmpool pre-reservation for Jul-week2. Capacity ops run smoke tests on pre-provisioned reserved pools.
- Week 2 (Jul 8–14): NA wave1 activation (300 GPUs live). Route canaries: 10% traffic to new capacity for 48 hours, auto-fallback enabled. Monitor 99th percentile latency, KV cache hit-rate, and batching efficiency.
- Week 3: NA warmpool sizing audit, EU procurement kickoff, APAC SKU checks.
- Week 4 (Jul 22–28): EU wave1 pre-reserve (160 GPUs) + NA wave2 planning.
- Week 6: NA wave2 activation (300 GPUs) + adjust warmpool based on wave1 telemetry.
- Week 8–12: EU wave activations in planned cadence. APAC preparatory checks.
- Month-by-month checkpoints: product readiness, SRE runbooks, private deployment verification (for Dedicated lanes).

Operational controls and automation items (actionable):
- Capacity-as-code templates for wave spin-ups (infra repo PRs required). Owner: Liam O'Connor.
- Metric gating rules for activation (must pass latency, error rate, and cold-start tail checks at canary stage). Owner: Maya Singh.
- Warmpool automated top-up implementation (tied to cost threshold and utilization triggers). Owner: Priya Patel.

Risk register / open questions:
- SKU substitutions: what SLAs do we accept if H100 not available in APAC for planned windows? (open)
- Vendor lead-time variability: contingency vendor lanes and cross-region burst costs need a cap in cost modeling (open).
- Customer communication: draft template for notifying Dedicated customers about staged onboarding and potential initial cross-region routing (action item).

Appendix (quick tables - text view):
1) Regional summary table (region | planned GPUs | warmpool % | warmpool GPUs | earliest activation):
   NA | 1200 | 16% | 192 | Jul-week2
   EU | 640 | 20% | 128 | Jul-week4
   APAC | 480 | 18% | 86 | Aug-week2

2) Activation gating checklist (must be TRUE to flip traffic to new pool):
   - health checks green for 48h
   - KV cache warm threshold >= 75% after warm-up
   - 99th p50 latency within 12% of Canary baseline
   - Rollback path validated and tested

Next steps / immediate asks:
- Infra ops: finalize PRs for NA wave1 capacity-as-code by Jul 5.
- Vendor management: confirm final SKU shipments for EU region by Jul 10.
- Product: prepare canary prompts and load shape definitions by Jul 8.

Notes to reviewers: This is a draft-run sheet intended to be pragmatic (mix of cost and reliability). Please call out any missed compliance constraints for EU/private lanes or additional headroom requests for mid-tier enterprise customers.

Document history: created 2026-06-12 by Ethan Zhang; updated 2026-07-01 to incorporate APAC vendor feedback and adjust warmpool percentages.
